title: Vocabulary, Figures of Speech and Editing
summary: Word formation, denotation and connotation, register, figures of speech in non-literary texts, commonly confused words, and proofreading and editing a text.

rows: un + believable → unbelievable; mis + inform → misinform
govern + ment → government; hope + less → hopeless
load + shedding → load-shedding; head + line → headline
SARS, NSFAS, CCMA (pronounced as words or letters)

items: **Register**: the level of formality. Formal: 'We regret to inform you…'; informal: 'Sorry, guys…'.
**Euphemism**: a mild expression for something unpleasant ('passed away').
**Jargon**: specialised language of a group (legal, medical).

notes.text: Figures of speech in everyday texts

Advertisers and journalists use **puns** ('Fresh ideas are brewing' for a coffee shop), **alliteration** ('Big Bargain Bonanza'), **hyperbole**, **rhetorical questions** and **metaphor** ('a tsunami of complaints').

notes.title: Choosing the correct word
notes.problem: Choose: 'The new rule will (affect/effect) everyone and its (affect/effect) will be serious.'
notes.answer: 'The new rule will affect everyone and its effect will be serious.'

items: Read the whole passage first for meaning.
Check punctuation, including apostrophes and commas.
Look for redundancy (e.g. 'return back', 'free gift') and tautology.

notes.title: Editing example
notes.problem: Correct: 'The principle said that the new rules will effect all learners, and that there phones must be stationery during lessons.'
steps: will effect → would affect (reported speech and correct word)
notes.answer: The principal said that the new rules would affect all learners, and that their phones must be stationary during lessons.
